mainTopic: Why the כהן גדול's separation before יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש on its source (the מילואים or סיני).
overview: The גמרא is explaining why the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול is learned from the מילואים only for יום הכפורים. Its first reason is that in both cases the כהן brings his bull from his own property. It then asks how this works for the view that "קח לך" means community property. It quotes the ברייתא of רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן, along with אבא חנן. The answer is that the dispute covers only ordinary cases. For the מילואים and יום הכפורים, the verses make clear that the bull is the כהן's own. רב אשי and רבינא then give other reasons the comparison fits only יום הכפורים: the matching offerings, the service of the כהן גדול, and a 'first service in a place'. Next, רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן learns only יום הכפורים from the מילואים verse, while רבי יהושע בן לוי also learns the פרה אדומה, and the גמרא defends רבי יוחנן's view against two challenges. Finally, ריש לקיש argues that the source cannot be the מילואים, since then every detail would be essential. He learns six days of separation from סיני instead, and explains the משנה's seven days as following רבי יהודה בן בתירא, whose concern is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: What about the opinion that 'take for you' means community property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its point that "עשה לך" means 'from your own.' Then it asks how its distinction works for the opinion that this wording means 'from the community.'
steps.simpleTranslation: "Make for you" means from your own property. But according to the one who says it means from community property, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's earlier distinction depended on "קח לך" / "עשה לך" meaning 'from your own property.' Now it challenges that distinction from the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "לך" means 'yours,' then the מילואים and יום הכפורים offerings are special because the כהן pays for them himself. But some say "לך" still means the community pays. On that view, these offerings would be just like all the others, and the distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
What is there to say? (how do we answer?)

steps.confusionAlert: The first words ("עשה לך — משלך") are not a new statement. They finish the גמרא's earlier argument. The real new move is the question that starts with "אלא".

phrases.english: "Make for you" means from your own,
but according to the one who said it means from community property,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction the גמרא made on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between the מילואים/יום הכפורים offerings and other offerings, which is built on 'קח לך = משלך'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'לך' does not mean the individual pays, these offerings would also be communal, and nothing would set them apart.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יאשיה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows the dispute exists. רבי יאשיה says "take for you" and "make for you" mean your own property, while "they shall take to you" means community property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "Take for you" means from your own; "make for you" means from your own; "and they shall take to you" means from the community. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that there really is an opinion that "לך" means community property. It starts with רבי יאשיה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה reads the wording literally. When the command is to משה ("for you"), משה pays. When the command is to the people ("they shall take"), the community pays. This is the view the גמרא's earlier distinction relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall take to you

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Take for you" means from your own,
and "make for you" means from your own,
"and they shall take to you" means from community property,
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the opinion mentioned in the question.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a dispute about whether 'לך' means one's own property.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: both mean community property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says both "take for you" and "they shall take to you" mean community property. "For you" only expresses God's affection for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: Both "take for you" and "they shall take to you" mean from community property. So why does the verse say "take for you"? As if to say: I want it from yours more than from theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the ברייתא. רבי יונתן is the opinion behind the question in Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יונתן, "לך" does not mean ownership or payment. It means God considers משה's part especially dear, so the item is described as if it were משה's. In practice the community still pays.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches / why does the verse say
As it were (used when describing God in human terms)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יונתן does not say "take for you" is meaningless. He says it expresses love or preference, not who pays.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין ״קַח לְךָ״, בֵּין ״וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ״ — מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: both "take for you" and "they shall take to you" mean from community property,
and why then does the verse say "take for you"?
As it were: I desire that it be from yours
more than from theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both phrasings mean community property. "לך" expresses God's special preference for משה.

steps.title: אבא חנן: the two verses about the ארון
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנן, in the name of רבי אלעזר, resolves two verses about who makes the ארון. It is attributed to the people when they do God's will, and to משה when they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר: One verse says "And make for you an ark of wood," and another verse says "And they shall make an ark of acacia wood." How can both be true? One refers to a time when Israel does God's will. The other refers to a time when they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third voice. It also reads "for you" as being about honor or credit, not about who pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון was made by the people. Still, one verse says "make for you" (משה). אבא חנן explains that when Israel does God's will, the credit goes to them. When they don't, the credit goes to משה alone. So here too, "לך" does not mean 'from your own money,' which adds weight to the question in Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (how do we reconcile them?)

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Abba Chanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״וְעָשִׂיתָ לְּךָ אֲרוֹן עֵץ״,
phrases.english: One verse says: "And make for you an ark of wood,"

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״וְעָשׂוּ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים״,
phrases.english: and one verse says: "And they shall make an ark of acacia wood."
How is this?

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Here, when Israel does the will of God;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם!
phrases.english: there, when they do not do the will of God!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another view in which "לך" is about credit, not ownership.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Make for you" and "they shall make" describe the same communal ארון. Who gets credit depends on whether Israel is doing God's will.

steps.title: The dispute is only about ordinary cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנאים disagree only about ordinary uses of "take for you" and "make for you," like spices and trumpets. In the מילואים and יום הכפורים, the verses clearly say the offering is from the כהן's own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about ordinary takings and ordinary makings. Ordinary takings: "Take for you spices." Ordinary makings: "Make for you two silver trumpets." But in these cases, the verses explicitly say it is from your own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 1 by limiting how far the dispute reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יונתן agrees that a verse can clearly mean 'from your own.' He only reads plain "לך" as communal in ordinary cases where nothing else points the other way. In the מילואים and יום הכפורים, the context makes it explicit, so the distinction holds according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to here (limits a dispute)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. A dispute is limited to general cases, so that a specific case can be agreed upon by everyone.

phrases.english: They only disagree
about ordinary takings and ordinary makings.
Ordinary takings: "Take for you spices."

phrases.aramaic: עֲשִׂיּוֹת דְּעָלְמָא — ״עֲשֵׂה לְךָ שְׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת כֶּסֶף״.
phrases.english: Ordinary makings: "Make for you two silver trumpets."
But in these cases, it explicitly states
that it is from your own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 1 after the sources were brought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יונתן reads "לך" as communal, the מילואים and יום הכפורים offerings would also be communal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute only covers ordinary cases. In the מילואים and יום הכפורים, the verses clearly mean the כהן's own property.

steps.title: Proof from the wording of the inauguration commands
steps.stepSummary: In the מילואים, the people are told "Take a goat," while אהרן is told "Take for you a calf." The contrast proves that here "for you" means from אהרן's own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the מילואים: since it is written, "And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Take a goat for a sin-offering," why do I need "And he said to אהרן: Take for you a calf for a sin-offering"? Learn from this that "take for you" means from your own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where the verse 'explicitly' says the offering is the כהן's own, as claimed in Step 5. It does this for the מילואים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives separate commands to the people and to אהרן, each with different wording. If everything came from the community, there would be no need for a separate "take for you" to אהרן. The contrast shows that אהרן's offering is his own, so even רבי יונתן would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The inauguration days of the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: Whether "קח לך" means 'your own' is disputed in ordinary cases. In the מילואים (and יום הכפורים), the context shows that the כהן brings the offering from his own property, according to everyone.

phrases.english: Regarding the inauguration: since it is written:
"And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying:
Take a goat for a sin-offering,"
then "And he said to Aaron:

phrases.aramaic: קַח לְךָ עֵגֶל בֶּן בָּקָר לְחַטָּאת״
phrases.english: Take for you a young calf for a sin-offering"
why do I need it?
Learn from this: "take for you" means from your own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the claim in Step 5 that the verses are explicit, using the מילואים.
steps.raayaObject: That in the מילואים, "קח לך" means from אהרן's own property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between ויקרא ט:ב ("קח לך" to אהרן) and ויקרא ט:ג ("קחו" to the people).

steps.title: Proof that on יום הכפורים the bull comes from the כהן גדול's own property
steps.stepSummary: The verses on יום הכפורים already say אהרן comes with a bull, and that the goats come from the people. The extra words 'his bull' must teach that the bull is from his own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום הכפורים: the Torah already wrote 'With this אהרן shall come into the holy place, with a young bull for a חטאת', and 'from the congregation of the children of Israel he shall take two goats for a חטאת'. So why do I need the words 'and he shall offer the bull of the חטאת which is his'? Learn from this that this 'his' means it comes from his own property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the second half of the answer from step 5. Just like in the מילואים, the יום הכפורים bull must come from the כהן גדול's own money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already told us that אהרן brings a bull, so repeating 'the bull which is his' seems unnecessary. Also, the goats are clearly marked as coming from the people. So the extra word 'his' must tell us something new: the bull is paid for by the כהן גדול himself. This makes יום הכפורים match the מילואים, which is why the comparison works only for יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / now, seeing that (it is already written)
The congregation of the children of Israel (the community)
Why do I need it? (this seems extra)

steps.whatToRemember: Both the מילואים and יום הכפורים have a bull paid for by the כהן himself. That shared feature is why the comparison points to יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the first answer for why the 7-day separation of the כהן גדול applies before יום הכפורים and not before other holidays.

phrases.english: And regarding Yom Kippur, since it is already written:
"With this Aaron shall come into the Sanctuary
with a young bull for a sin-offering, etc. ...
And from the congregation of the children of Israel
he shall take two goats for a sin-offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:ה. The goats are clearly community property.

phrases.english: "And he shall offer the bull of the sin-offering which is his"
Why do I need this?
phrases.notes: The bull was already mentioned, so 'which is his' seems extra.

phrases.english: Learn from it: this word 'his' means it is from his own property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel proof to step 6. Step 6 proved the מילואים case, and this step proves the יום הכפורים case.
steps.raayaObject: That the יום הכפורים bull comes from the כהן גדול's own property
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא טז:ג, טז:ה–ו, where the extra word 'לו' contrasts with the goats from the community

steps.title: רב אשי: both days have a bull for a sin-offering and a ram for a burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason why the מילואים connect to יום הכפורים. Both have exactly a bull for a חטאת and a ram for an עולה. On ראש השנה and עצרת, both animals are עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We learn 'a bull for a חטאת and a ram for an עולה' from 'a bull for a חטאת and a ram for an עולה'. This leaves out ראש השנה and עצרת, where both of them are עולות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another way to explain why the comparison points to יום הכפורים and not to other holidays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offerings in the מילואים and on יום הכפורים have the same pattern: a bull as a חטאת and a ram as an עולה. ראש השנה and עצרת also have a bull and a ram, but both are brought as עולות. So the pattern does not match, and those days are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / compare (one case from another)
A bull for a sin-offering and a ram for a burnt-offering

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We derive a bull for a sin-offering and a ram for a burnt-offering (Yom Kippur)
from a bull for a sin-offering and a ram for a burnt-offering (the inauguration),
to exclude Rosh Hashana and Shavuot,
where both of them (the bull and the ram) are burnt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer instead of the 'own property' answer of steps 5–7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the comparison could apply to ראש השנה or עצרת, which also have a bull and a ram.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only יום הכפורים matches the exact pattern of the מילואים: a חטאת bull and an עולה ram.

steps.title: רבינא: both are services done only by the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says we compare a service done only by the כהן גדול to another service done only by the כהן גדול. This leaves out all the other days that were suggested, because any כהן may do their service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We learn a service done by the כהן גדול from a service done by the כהן גדול. This leaves out all the other days raised in the questions, because they are not services that need a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a third reason why the comparison points only to יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מילואים service was done by אהרן, the כהן גדול. The יום הכפורים service also must be done by the כהן גדול. On all the other days suggested earlier, a regular כהן can do the service. So they do not match, and all the earlier questions are answered at once.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
We derive a service done by the High Priest (Yom Kippur)
from a service done by the High Priest (the inauguration),
to exclude all the cases raised in the questions,
since they are not services that require the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר דָּנִין עֲבוֹדָה בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative answer, alongside רב אשי's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Other days with special offerings might also be compared to the מילואים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only יום הכפורים, like the מילואים, needs the כהן גדול himself to do the service.

steps.title: Another version of רבינא: a first service from a first service
steps.stepSummary: Some report רבינא differently. He compares a 'first service' to a 'first service', and this leaves out days whose service is not 'first'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say that רבינא said: We learn a first service from a first service. This leaves out these other days, because they are not 'first'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבינא said. It is unclear what 'first' means, so the גמרא will ask about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version uses a new idea, 'first service' (תחלה), instead of 'service of the כהן גדול'. The meaning is not yet explained. This step sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: And some say that Ravina said:
We derive a first service from a first service,
to exclude these (other days), which are not 'first'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רבינא's answer from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The comparison works because both the מילואים and יום הכפורים are a 'first service'.

steps.title: What does 'first' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבינא means by 'first service'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'first' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the unclear word 'first' in the second version of רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'first' could mean different things. The גמרא wants a definition that actually adds something new to רבינא's first version.

phrases.english: What does 'first' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key word in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'תחלה' in רבינא's second version

steps.title: It cannot mean 'first' as in done by the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: If 'first' meant a service by the כהן גדול, this version would be the same as the first version. So that cannot be the meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'first' means done by the כהן גדול, that is the same as the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'איכא דאמרי' should be a real second version, not the same idea in new words. If 'first' only meant 'by the כהן גדול', the two versions would say the same thing. So the גמרא looks for a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposed answer that will be rejected)
That is the same as the first one

phrases.english: If you say 'first' means a service by the High Priest,
that is the same as the first version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question of step 11 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only one reading of 'תחלה', not רבינא's second version itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading makes the second version the same as the first version

steps.title: 'First' means the first service in a special place
steps.stepSummary: 'First' means the first service in a place. יום הכפורים has the special service in the קודש הקדשים, and the מילואים was the first service in the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: we learn a first service in a place from a first service in a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of 'first' in רבינא's second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, the כהן גדול serves in the קודש הקדשים, where no service is done all year, so it is like a 'first' service there. The מילואים was the first service ever done in the משכן. Both are a beginning of service in a place, and the other days are not.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place (the קודש הקדשים / the משכן)

steps.whatToRemember: There are several reasons the מילואים connect to יום הכפורים: the bull is from the כהן's own property, the offering pattern matches (רב אשי), the כהן גדול does the service (רבינא), or both are a 'first service in a place' (רבינא, second version).
steps.confusionAlert: 'First' here does not mean first in time during the day, and it does not mean 'done by the כהן גדול'. It means the beginning of service in a special place.

phrases.english: Rather, we derive a first service in the place (the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur)
from a first service in the place (the Tabernacle at the inauguration).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 12 rejected the first proposal.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תחלה' means the first service in a special place: the קודש הקדשים on יום הכפורים, and the משכן at the מילואים.

steps.title: רב דימי reports how many cases each אמורא learns from the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a disagreement. רבי יוחנן learns one case from the מילואים verse (יום הכפורים). רבי יהושע בן לוי learns two (the פרה אדומה and יום הכפורים).
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: רבי יוחנן teaches one case, and רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches two. רבי יוחנן teaches one: 'to do, to atone' means the services of יום הכפורים. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches two: 'to do' means the services of the פרה, and 'to atone' means the services of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report arrives from ארץ ישראל. It tells us how two great אמוראים read the words 'to do, to atone' in the מילואים verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'לעשות לכפר' as one phrase that points only to יום הכפורים. רבי יהושע בן לוי splits it into two words, giving two cases: 'לעשות' points to the פרה and 'לכפר' points to יום הכפורים. Both cases then need the seven-day separation, just like the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel
'To do, to atone', words from the מילואים verse
The service of burning the red heifer (פרה אדומה)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Rabbi Yochanan teaches one,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi teaches two.
Rabbi Yochanan teaches one:
"To do, to atone":
these are the services of Yom Kippur.
And Yehoshua ben Levi teaches two:
"To do": these are the services of the heifer,
"To atone": these are the services of Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from רבינא's comparisons to a new report about how the מילואים verse is read.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: only יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים. רבי יהושע בן לוי: both the פרה and יום הכפורים are learned from it.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה that mentions separation before the heifer too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. The משנה clearly mentions a seven-day separation before the פרה as well, so how can he learn only one case?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוחנן really teach only one? But we learned in the משנה: seven days before יום הכפורים, and seven days before the burning of the פרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view using the משנה. The משנה lists two separations, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the פרה separation exactly like the יום הכפורים separation. That makes it look like both come from the same Torah source. This seems to fit רבי יהושע בן לוי and not רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The burning of the red heifer

phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yochanan teach only one?
But we learned:
Seven days before Yom Kippur,
and seven days before the burning of the heifer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's 'one case' position from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that only יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists a separation before the פרה as well, which suggests a Torah source for two cases.

steps.title: The heifer separation is only an extra stringency
steps.stepSummary: The separation before the פרה is only a rabbinic מעלה (an added level of care). It is not learned from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is merely an extra stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The פרה separation in the משנה is real, but the רבנן added it. It is not from the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the משנה does not prove that the Torah requires two separations. רבי יוחנן still learns only יום הכפורים from the מילואים, and the פרה rule comes from the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely an extra stringency (added by the רבנן)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean there is no separation before the פרה. There is one. Its source is rabbinic and not from the מילואים verse.

phrases.english: It is merely an extra stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source: the rule is rabbinic, not from the Torah.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's separation before the פרה comes from the מילואים verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separation before the פרה is a rabbinic stringency, so רבי יוחנן's 'one case' stands.

steps.title: Challenge from a teaching in רבי יוחנן's own name
steps.stepSummary: A chain of tradition quotes רבי יוחנן himself as learning both the פרה and יום הכפורים from the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מניומי בר חלקיה said that רבי מחסיא בר אידי said that רבי יוחנן said: 'As He did this day, so ה׳ commanded to do, to atone for you.' 'To do' means the services of the פרה, and 'to atone' means the services of יום הכפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. Here רבי יוחנן himself is quoted as teaching two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This quote matches רבי יהושע בן לוי's two-case reading word for word. It directly contradicts רב דימי's report that רבי יוחנן teaches only one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As He did this day', the מילואים verse (ויקרא ח:לד)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי מִנְיוֹמֵי בַּר חִלְקִיָּה
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Minyomi bar Chilkiya say
that Rabbi Machseya bar Idi said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
"As He has done this day,
so the Lord commanded to do, to atone for you";
"To do": these are the services of the heifer,
"To atone": these are the services of Yom Kippur!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי מִנְיוֹמֵי בַּר חִלְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבי יוחנן's 'one case' view, this time from his own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's report of רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another tradition quotes רבי יוחנן as teaching two cases, which contradicts the report that he teaches one.

steps.title: That teaching was his teacher's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was only repeating his teacher's opinion. He did not hold it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the view of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two-case teaching quoted in רבי יוחנן's name really belongs to his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passing on a teacher's opinion is not the same as agreeing with it. רבי יוחנן's own view stays 'one case'.

keyTerms.meaning: That is [the view] of his teacher

phrases.english: That is the view of his teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the statement is the teacher's view, which the student was only reporting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The quoted teaching is רבי יוחנן's own opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was quoting his teacher. He himself teaches only one case.

steps.title: רבין's report proves it came from רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן said the two-case reading in the name of רבי ישמעאל. This proves it was his teacher's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: 'to do' means the services of the פרה, and 'to atone' means the services of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the previous answer. A fuller version of the same teaching shows that רבי יוחנן was quoting רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מניומי's version left out the original source. רבין's version names רבי ישמעאל, so the two-case reading is his and not רבי יוחנן's.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's own view: only יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים. The פרה separation is rabbinic, and the two-case reading belongs to רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: For when Ravin came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
"To do": these are the services of the heifer,
"To atone": these are the services of Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives evidence for the re-attribution in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the two-case reading is his teacher's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report that רבי יוחנן said it in the name of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: then every detail should be required
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן. If the separation is learned from the מילואים, then just as every written detail of the מילואים was required, every detail here should be required too.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: From where do you learn this? From the מילואים. If so, just as with the מילואים everything written about them was required (missing any detail made it invalid), so too here, everything written about them should be required.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. ריש לקיש pushes on how far the comparison to the מילואים goes. His challenge sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the מילואים, missing any detail made the whole thing fail. If יום הכפורים copies the מילואים, every detail of the separation should also be essential. That would be a very strict result, and the גמרא will need to address it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you learn it?
The seven-day inauguration of the משכן and כהנים
Is essential; without it the act is invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the question of whether learning from a source means copying all of its strict details. That question shapes the rest of the sugya.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
From where do you derive it?
From the inauguration;
if so, just as with the inauguration
everything written about them is essential to them,
so too here as well,
everything written about them should be essential to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מֵהֵיכָא קָא יָלְפַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים, and challenges what follows from that.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's derivation of the separation from the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison should carry over the source's rules. Since every written detail of the מילואים was essential, every detail here should be essential too.

steps.title: The backup priest is never separated
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש blocks the reply that the פרישה really is required. The משנה says they only 'prepare' a backup כהן. It never says they separate him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: yes, that is true, the separation really is required. But we learned in the משנה: 'And they prepare another כהן for him.' It does not say 'they separate' him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש expects רבי יוחנן to answer, 'Yes, the separation is required.' He knocks that answer down with the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The backup כהן might end up doing the יום הכפורים service. Yet the משנה never says he is separated for seven days. So the separation cannot be something that makes the service invalid when it is missing. That means it cannot be learned from the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say' – the גמרא brings up a possible answer in order to reject it
'Yes, indeed so' – accepting the challenge's point
'They separate' (move him away from his home)

steps.confusionAlert: 'הכי נמי' here is not the גמרא agreeing. It is an answer that ריש לקיש imagines רבי יוחנן giving, and he immediately rejects it.

phrases.english: And if you say: indeed so (it really is required),
but we learned: 'And they prepare another priest for him,'
phrases.notes: From the first משנה of יומא.

phrases.english: and it does not teach 'they separate'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's challenge from step 20 and shuts down a possible way out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרישה is learned from the מילואים, and so is required.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The backup כהן is not separated, yet he can serve. So separation is not required. That cannot fit a source from the מילואים, where every detail was required.

steps.title: 'Prepare' cannot mean 'separate'
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say that 'מתקינין' simply means 'מפרישין'. That reading is rejected: the משנה would then use one word for both כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: what does 'they prepare' mean? It means 'they separate.' If so, the משנה should use the same word for both. Either say 'prepare' for both, or say 'separate' for both.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש blocks a second way out. Someone could claim the word 'prepare' secretly means 'separate.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses 'מפרישין' for the כהן גדול and a different word, 'מתקינין', for the backup. Changing the word shows the two are treated differently. So the backup is truly not separated, and ריש לקיש's challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it teach' – the משנה should have said...
'This one and that one' – both cases

phrases.english: And if you say: what is 'they prepare'? It means 'they separate,'
then let it teach either 'they prepare' for both,
or 'they separate' for both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible defense against the challenge in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that 'מתקינין' means the same thing as 'מפרישין'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deliberately uses two different words. That shows two different actions.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this step, ריש לקיש's attack on learning the פרישה from the מילואים is complete.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks for ריש לקיש's source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן turns to ריש לקיש and asks where he himself learns the פרישה from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: then where do you, Master, learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: Since ריש לקיש rejected the מילואים, רבי יוחנן asks for his alternative source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion now moves from attacking one source to finding another. Everyone agrees there is a פרישה. The question is only where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather / so then' – shifting to a new direction

phrases.english: He (רבי יוחנן) said to him: rather, you, Master,
from where do you derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶלָּא מָר מֵהֵיכָא יָלֵיף לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to ריש לקיש's challenge by asking for his own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: ריש לקיש's own source for the פרישה before יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The source is סיני: six days of separation
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns it from הר סיני. The cloud covered for six days, and משה was called on the seventh. That teaches that anyone entering the camp of the שכינה needs six days of separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: from סיני, as it says: 'The glory of ה׳ rested on הר סיני, and the cloud covered it six days, and He called to משה on the seventh day.' Since it already says 'He called to משה on the seventh day,' why mention 'six days'? This is a model (בנין אב): anyone who enters the camp of the שכינה needs six days of separation.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his source. משה waited six days before he was called into the cloud, and this teaches a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the seventh day' already tells us that six days passed. So the extra words 'six days' must teach something. They teach that six days of preparation come before entering a holy place. The כהן גדול entering the קודש הקדשים is like that. Since this comes from סיני and not the מילואים, it does not need to follow every detail of the מילואים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since / after all' – pointing out that something is already stated
A model case from which a general rule is built
The camp (area) of the Divine Presence

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן learns the פרישה from the מילואים (seven days). ריש לקיש learns it from סיני (six days).

phrases.english: He said: from Sinai, as it is written:
'And the glory of the Lord rested on Mount Sinai,'
'and the cloud covered it six days,'
'and He called to Moses on the seventh day.'

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב: ״וַיִּקְרָא אֶל מֹשֶׁה בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי״,
phrases.english: Now, since it is written: 'and He called to Moses on the seventh day,'
what do the words 'six days' come to teach?
This set up a general rule:
that anyone who enters the camp of the Divine Presence
requires six days of separation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פרישה is learned from סיני. The extra words 'six days' teach six days of separation before entering the camp of the שכינה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because this source is not the מילואים, ריש לקיש avoids his own challenge. Nothing requires that every detail be followed.

steps.title: But the משנה says seven days
steps.stepSummary: The source from סיני gives six days. But the משנה says the כהן גדול is separated for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned seven in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's source. It produces the wrong number of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיני teaches six days, yet the משנה clearly says seven. So ריש לקיש must explain where the extra day comes from.

phrases.english: But we learned seven (days) in the mishna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number of days that ריש לקיש's source gives in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's source from סיני (six days).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires seven days, but סיני only gives six.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He adds a day because of a special concern. That concern is explained on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who is concerned...
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains the seventh day. The משנה follows one specific תנא, who adds a day out of worry. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah source still gives six days. The seventh day is an extra precaution from רבי יהודה בן בתירא. So the משנה's 'seven' does not disprove the source from סיני.
steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of the sentence. What he is worried about is explained right after this.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הִיא,
phrases.english: The mishna is (the view of) Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
who is concerned...

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven days in the משנה seemed to contradict a six-day source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires six days. רבי יהודה בן בתירא adds a seventh day as a precaution, and the משנה follows him.
